Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

```python
from sceneact import *
import bpy, math, random
from mathutils import Vector

random.seed(16)
scene = Scene('Quiet timber hall')

ivory = (.73,.74,.69)
wood = (.46,.48,.42)
lightwood = (.66,.68,.61)
floorcolor = (.78,.79,.74)
dark = (.20,.22,.19)

def add(name, obj):
    scene.include(name, obj)
    return obj

add('continuous pale floor', box((32,32,.16), center=(0,2,-.08), color=floorcolor))
add('rear plaster wall', box((27,.22,7.4), center=(0,10,3.7), color=ivory))
add('right plaster wall', box((.22,23,7.4), center=(9,0,3.7), color=ivory))
add('left plaster wall', box((.22,23,7.4), center=(-12,0,3.7), color=ivory))
add('rear skirting', box((27,.065,.12), center=(0,9.84,.06), color=(.28,.29,.23)))
add('right skirting', box((.065,23,.12), center=(8.84,0,.06), color=(.28,.29,.23)))

# A shallow recess beneath the transverse timber lintel.
add('recess right return', box((.16,3.4,3.15), center=(5.5,8.25,1.575), color=ivory))
add('return baseboard', box((.045,3.4,.12), center=(5.39,8.25,.06), color=(.28,.29,.23)))
add('transverse deep timber lintel', box((27,.73,.91), center=(0,6.25,4.18), color=wood))
add('lower pale lintel edge', box((27,.77,.12), center=(0,6.23,3.68), color=lightwood))

# Closely spaced timber boards on the roof.
for j in range(63):
    y = -10 + j*.34
    add('roof plank %02d'%j,
        box((27,.332,.115), center=(0,y,7.04),
            color=(.68+random.uniform(-.035,.035),
                   .69+random.uniform(-.035,.035),
                   .63+random.uniform(-.035,.035))))
    for x in (-10,-6,-2,2,6,10):
        if random.random() < .73:
            add('roof nail %s %s'%(j,x),
                rod(.012, start=(x,y,6.975), end=(x,y,6.965), color=(.29,.30,.26)))

# Slim beams supporting the boarded ceiling.
for x in (-9,3.5,9):
    add('ceiling longitudinal rib %s'%x,
        box((.18,24,.34), center=(x,1,6.81), color=wood))

# The dominant laminated tree support is made of continuous adjacent
# strips, each following the same curved structural profile.
def beam_strip(name, points, width, depth, color):
    part = Asset(name)
    for k,(a,b) in enumerate(zip(points[:-1], points[1:])):
        dx,dy,dz = b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1],b[2]-a[2]
        length = math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz)
        node = box((width,depth,length+.018),
                   center=((a[0]+b[0])/2,(a[1]+b[1])/2,(a[2]+b[2])/2),
                   color=color)
        node.turn('y', math.degrees(math.atan2(dx,dz)))
        part.include(str(k),node)
    add(name,part)

base_x=-3.0
for strip in range(11):
    off=(strip-5)*.067
    c=(.40+random.uniform(-.035,.035),
       .43+random.uniform(-.035,.035),
       .37+random.uniform(-.035,.035))
    # Right arm sweeps outward gently at the foot and widely overhead.
    pts=[]
    for k in range(43):
        t=k/42
        z=.11+7.18*t
        x=base_x+off+5.8*(t**3.1)
        pts.append((x,0,z))
    beam_strip('right arch lamination %02d'%strip,pts,.066,.73,c)

    # Left arm rises into the opposing ceiling bay.
    pts=[]
    for k in range(43):
        t=k/42
        z=.11+7.18*t
        x=base_x+off-2.6*(t**2.5)
        pts.append((x,.015,z))
    beam_strip('left arch lamination %02d'%strip,pts,.066,.71,c)

add('dark foot collar', box((.79,.79,.16),center=(base_x,0,.08),color=(.25,.27,.21)))

# Timber-clad jambs frame the broad opening.
for side,x0,x1 in [('left',-4.5,-2.55),('right',6.0,8.0)]:
    count=int((x1-x0)/.14)
    for i in range(count):
        x=x0+(i+.5)*(x1-x0)/count
        v=random.uniform(-.055,.045)
        add('%s vertical wall board %02d'%(side,i),
            box(((x1-x0)/count-.009,.19,3.63),
                center=(x,6.18,1.815),
                color=(.60+v,.62+v,.56+v)))

# Vent grilles set into the long horizontal timber fascia.
for i,(x,w) in enumerate([(-8.4,1.65),(-.4,1.45),(5.3,1.0)]):
    add('vent pale frame %d'%i, box((w+.09,.035,.35),center=(x,5.865,4.18),color=(.73,.74,.68)))
    add('vent dark inset %d'%i, box((w,.045,.265),center=(x,5.838,4.18),color=(.27,.29,.26)))
    for n in range(int(w/.10)):
        xx=x-w/2+.055+n*.10
        add('grille division %d %d'%(i,n),
            box((.011,.012,.25),center=(xx,5.808,4.18),color=(.50,.52,.46)))

for i,x in enumerate((-8.1,-4.8)):
    add('wall ventilation surround %d'%i,
        box((.90,.035,.29),center=(x,9.865,3.24),color=(.80,.81,.75)))
    add('wall ventilation shadow %d'%i,
        box((.76,.045,.20),center=(x,9.84,3.24),color=(.37,.39,.34)))
    for n in range(9):
        add('wall vent slat %d %d'%(i,n),
            box((.018,.012,.19),center=(x-.34+n*.083,9.809,3.24),color=lightwood))

# Small wall fittings and a narrow door on the right.
add('door inset',box((.83,.045,2.28),center=(5.00,9.855,1.14),color=(.64,.66,.60)))
for x in (4.56,5.44):
    add('door jamb '+str(x),box((.035,.055,2.32),center=(x,9.81,1.16),color=(.48,.51,.45)))
add('door head',box((.91,.055,.035),center=(5,9.81,2.32),color=(.48,.51,.45)))
add('door handle',box((.035,.06,.16),center=(5.31,9.765,1.06),color=(.27,.29,.26)))
add('exit sign',box((.29,.045,.17),center=(5,9.80,2.57),color=(.38,.43,.36)))
for x in (-1.3,3.5):
    add('low wall socket '+str(x),box((.075,.035,.06),center=(x,9.85,.16),color=(.28,.30,.26)))
add('wall utility panel',box((.38,.035,.25),center=(3.55,9.85,.54),color=(.67,.69,.63)))

# Suspended cylindrical pendant shades.
for i,(x,y,z,r) in enumerate([(0.3,2.9,5.25,.34),(7.8,4.2,5.13,.29)]):
    add('pendant suspension %d'%i,
        rod(.017,start=(x,y,z+.60),end=(x,y,6.92),color=(.24,.26,.22)))
    add('pendant ceiling rose %d'%i,
        rod(.075,start=(x,y,6.88),end=(x,y,6.96),color=(.35,.37,.31)))
    add('pendant cylindrical shade %d'%i,
        rod(r,start=(x,y,z-.50),end=(x,y,z+.55),color=(.37,.39,.33)))
    add('pendant bottom diffuser %d'%i,
        rod(r*.94,start=(x,y,z-.515),end=(x,y,z-.50),color=(.94,.95,.87)))

realize(scene)

# Subtle procedural grain gives the timber its washed, archival character.
for mat in bpy.data.materials:
    if not mat.use_nodes:
        mat.use_nodes=True
    bs=mat.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
    if bs:
        bs.inputs['Roughness'].default_value=.78

for ob in bpy.data.objects:
    if ob.type!='MESH':
        continue
    name=ob.name.lower()
    if any(s in name for s in ('lamination','plank','timber','board','rib')):
        for slot in ob.material_slots:
            mat=slot.material
            if not mat:
                continue
            mat.use_nodes=True
            nt=mat.node_tree
            bs=nt.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
            tex=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexNoise')
            tex.inputs['Scale'].default_value=4
            tex.inputs['Detail'].default_value=3
            coord=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeTexCoord')
            mapping=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeVectorMath')
            mapping.operation='MULTIPLY'
            mapping.inputs[1].default_value=(26,26,1.4)
            nt.links.new(coord.outputs['Generated'],mapping.inputs[0])
            nt.links.new(mapping.outputs[0],tex.inputs['Vector'])
            bump=nt.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBump')
            bump.inputs['Strength'].default_value=.18
            bump.inputs['Distance'].default_value=.025
            nt.links.new(tex.outputs['Fac'],bump.inputs['Height'])
            nt.links.new(bump.outputs['Normal'],bs.inputs['Normal'])

set_view((7.8,-15.0,3.65),(0.0,5.0,3.35),lens=35,sensor=36)
area_emitter((-6,-5,6.4),power=1800,size=8,target=(-1,4,0),color=(1,.99,.94))
area_emitter((5,-3,6.7),power=1300,size=7,target=(2,6,1),color=(.96,.98,1))
area_emitter((-8,6,5.3),power=700,size=5,target=(-3,3,1))
for x,y,z in [(0.3,2.9,4.72),(7.8,4.2,4.60)]:
    area_emitter((x,y,z),power=80,size=.55,target=(x,y,0),color=(1,1,.94))

world=bpy.context.scene.world
world.use_nodes=True
world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[0].default_value=(.77,.80,.75,1)
world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[1].default_value=.65
sc=bpy.context.scene
sc.render.engine='CYCLES'
sc.cycles.samples=48
sc.cycles.use_denoising=True
sc.render.resolution_x=512
sc.render.resolution_y=406
sc.render.resolution_percentage=100
sc.view_settings.view_transform='AgX'
sc.view_settings.exposure=.55
sc.view_settings.gamma=1.0
```
